title: KB3f: the vanishing-character restriction on the 18-point cover question for F2^7 (outcome=partial, no new kappa)
body:
# KB3f: the vanishing-character restriction pressed against the four surviving 18-point splits (outcome=partial, no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson) a restored seven-source singleton word is universal exactly when its prefix set `P` covers: `P + P = F2^7`. The 17-point question is closed ([PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542), [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634), [PR 2773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2773), [PR 2870](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2870), all Aaron Wang). [PR 2911](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2911) (Aaron Wang) narrowed the 18-point question to the splits `(12,6)`, `(11,7)`, `(10,8)`, `(9,9)` and PROVED that any `(12,6)` or `(10,8)` cover must have a vanishing character off the all-ones hyperplane.

This package (PR 2911's open questions 1-2) presses that restriction: it classifies the vanishing configurations exactly and tests each class against coverage of the remaining masks. Everything is exact integer arithmetic; no words are enumerated; the concurrent repeated-state `L = 20` word census (Nicholas Stone, [discussion 1166 comment 18954844](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954844)) is a different, word-level object and is untouched.

**Verdict: not decided, narrowed.** Six vanishing classes are PROVEN impossible, the two tight classes are pinned to exact forced Sidon structure, and for `(11,7)/(9,9)` the restriction provably cannot press at all. No split is excluded outright and no 18-point cover is constructed; the gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged.

## Classification lemmas (PROVEN, machine-checked)

- **L2 (halving).** `char_sum(A, psi) = 0` holds exactly when `A` splits `|A|/2 + |A|/2` across `ker(psi)`. So `A`-vanishing needs `s` even and forces `(s/2, s/2)`; `D`-vanishing needs `t` even and forces `(t/2, t/2)`. At `(11,7)` and `(9,9)` both sides are odd: **no character can vanish**, so the restriction is vacuous exactly on those two splits.
- **L3 (half-decomposition).** With `H = ker(psi)` and `H' = E` minus `H`, coverage decomposes into four exact half lines. Checked exhaustively over all `256 x 256` pairs `(A, D)` of `F2^3` and 4,000 random pairs of `F2^5`.
- **L4 (class floors).** Exact union-size bounds on the half lines: `a0*a1 + d0*d1 >= 32` and three sibling floors. In character language they re-derive PR 2911's even-half and odd-half bounds in split language; the class verdicts are their forced-split consequences.
- **L5 (multi-vanishing structure).** Two simultaneous vanishings force the balanced grid `(x, y, y, x)` with `x + y = |A|/2`. Exhaustive at `F2^3`.
- **L7 (equality analysis).** Floor equality plus coverage forces both cross sumsets Sidon and disjoint with union the whole odd half. Exhaustive at `F2^3`.

## Verdict per split (exact integers; mirrors identical by odd translation)

| Split | Forced vanishing (PR 2911, reproduced) | Vanishing classes after the floors | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(12,6)` | yes | A-vanish `(6,0)(5,1)(4,2)(3,3)` survive; D-vanish `(12,0)(11,1)(10,2)` PROVEN impossible; D-vanish `(9,3)(8,4)(7,5)(6,6)` survive | narrowed, not excluded |
| `(11,7)` | no vanishing exists (L2) | none | restriction does not press |
| `(10,8)` | yes | A-vanish `(8,0)` PROVEN impossible; `(7,1)` tight; `(6,2)(5,3)(4,4)` survive; D-vanish `(10,0)(9,1)` PROVEN impossible; `(8,2)` tight; `(7,3)(6,4)(5,5)` survive | narrowed, not excluded |
| `(9,9)` | no vanishing exists (L2) | none | restriction does not press |

Forced structure of the pinned classes: `(12,6)` A-vanish `(6,0)` forces `|A0+A1| = 32` (the whole odd half, 36 pairs, excess 4) with `A0 + D = H` and `A1 + D = H'` full; `(10,8)` A-vanish `(7,1)` forces `|A0+A1| = 25` and `|D0+D1| = 7` (both Sidon, disjoint, union 32); `(10,8)` D-vanish `(8,2)` forces `|A0+A1| = 16` (`A0` misses its own translate) and `|D0+D1| = 16` (a 4-by-4 Sidon pair), disjoint.

## Ground-truth census: which classes actually occur

Complete enumeration at the two smallest cover-bearing instances (independent route: every subset resp. every ten-set, not the predecessor's fixed-zero engine).

- `F2^4`: all 65,536 subsets scanned; 41,341 covers `S + S = F2^4`; classified by split and vanishing type.
- `F2^5`: all `C(32,10) = 64,512,240` ten-sets scanned; 317,440 covers total; the covers through the zero element number exactly 99,200, reproducing PR 2773's recorded n5 control value (99,200 x 32 / 10 = 317,440). Exact split support: `(2,8)` 15,360; `(4,6)` 143,360; `(6,4)` 143,360; `(8,2)` 15,360. No 10-cover of `F2^5` has split `(5,5)`, `(3,7)`, `(7,3)` or `(1,9)`, and every cover has vanishing characters on at least one side.
- Soundness: across all 358,781 covers of both censuses no cover hits a dead class; the floors reject no real configuration.

## Bounded class-restricted search (CHECKED; scoped search failure)

Smallest falsifying instance first: one covering pair `(A, D)` in a surviving class. Seeded first-improvement local search restricted to each of the 16 surviving classes (bit-0 `psi`, WLOG under `GL(6,2)`), 30 restarts each: no cover found; best scores 115 to 119 of 128 per class, consistent with PR 2911's unrestricted best 118/128. Non-vacuity: the identical machinery finds `F2^5` `(4,6)` covers instantly both free (`A=[9,12,13,14], D=[3,5,8,9,10,11]`) and inside the census-nonempty class A-vanish `(2,4)`. A failed bounded search is evidence about the searched domain, never an exclusion.

## Recorded anchors (reproduced before any new number)

PR 2542/2634 REPRO tiers `945/31`, `10395/49`, `945945/59` (records SHA-256 match) and the length-18 census `15,775,992` nodes / `312,064` cycles / `0` universal; PR 2870 OBSTRUCTION `parseval=696 allowed=504 deficit=192` both parity orders; PR 2911 SQUEEZE table, PROFILE18 spectra `16/22/50/31`, NOVANISH lines and ROWS18 `808/501/251/196`; the n5 set controls; and both heavy PR 2773 census anchors re-walked IN FULL from EMPTY receipts (`PASS_ANCHORS_K10B3 count=149990400`, `PASS_ANCHORS_K11B4 count=0`, 62/62 sub-shards each). `ANCHOR-REPRO.json` records every command and the receipt-validation correction (a replay against a committed receipt validates; the walks recorded here started from a missing receipt file).

## Reproduce

Standard library only, CPython 3.12, from the repository root (package `research/f7-18point-vanishing-seedfc618722/`):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-vanishing-seedfc618722/test_engine.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-vanishing-seedfc618722/verify.py quick
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-vanishing-seedfc618722/verify.py novanish
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-vanishing-seedfc618722/verify.py classify
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-vanishing-seedfc618722/verify.py search
```

Expected markers: `Ran 14 tests ... OK`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_QUICK`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_NOVANISH`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_CLASSIFY`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_SEARCH`. The heavy anchors are re-walked by the byte-vendored `anchors.py` (resumable, per-sub-shard receipts; `run_anchors_all.py` loops both modes).

## Scope and limitations

Set-level only inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: anything word-level, the 19-point cover question, walk-realizability of any cover, and any kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier implication. The surviving classes are not proved nonempty or empty: the class floors and Sidon pinning are necessary conditions, and the class-restricted search failures are bounded search failures. The tight classes' exact decision is the open step (README open question 1). The gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged.
